title: Air-Gap TX Signer
summary: Air-gapped Ethereum transaction signer for Raspberry Pi Pico: host builds an unsigned Sepolia tx, the Pico holds the key and signs offline over USB after Confirm/Cancel. Desktop C crypto path (Keccak-256 + secp256k1) already passes known-answer tests; firmware and device UX wait on hardware arrival. Learning/demo signer, not a Ledger replacement.

caseStudy.problem: I want a physically confirmable, air-gapped way to sign Ethereum transactions for learning and demo use, without putting a private key on a networked host.
ownership: Portable Keccak-256 and secp256k1 path in C, verified against Python/Ethereum reference vectors
Host tooling to build unsigned Sepolia transactions, assemble signed raw txs, and talk USB serial
Firmware protocol design for PING/PONG, GET_ADDR, and confirm-gated SIGN
architecture: Host builds the unsigned transaction and signing digest
Pico holds the key, shows a summary, waits for Confirm/Cancel, returns r/s/v over USB
Host attaches the signature and can broadcast to Sepolia
Pico stays offline: no Wi-Fi or networking
decisions: Use Ethereum Keccak-256, not NIST SHA3-256
Keep Python as the reference generator and C as the implementation under test
Scaffold firmware protocol before wiring LCD, buttons, or RP2040 secp256k1
verification: desktop test harness against vectors/known_answers.json: ALL PASS
Known-answer coverage for Keccak, key derivation, Ethereum address, recoverable ECDSA, and a legacy Sepolia signing hash
limitations: Pico firmware is a scaffold only until hardware arrives
RP2040/libsecp256k1 port is not validated yet
Demo key in vectors is public and must never be funded
Testnet/learning use only, not a mainnet-safe wallet
productionDifferences: Future hardware path: blink/USB hello, LCD + buttons, crypto port, confirm UX, then Sepolia end-to-end
